message:
I keep getting stuck in a loop. Let me just write the trace file using a simple heredoc and submit it:

<function=execute_bash>
<parameter=command>
printf '%s' '[{"step":1,"file":"fuzz-libdwfl.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":31,"var":"data","code":"fwrite(data, size, 1, fp)","note":"Attacker-controlled input bytes are written to a temp file that will be opened as an archive."},{"step":2,"file":"fuzz-libdwfl.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":39,"var":"mod","code":"dwfl_report_offline(dwfl, filename, filename, -1)","note":"The temp file is reported as an offline module, causing libdwfl to open it with elf_begin."},{"step":3,"file":"libelf/elf_begin.c","function":"dup_elf","line":1061,"var":"ref","code":"__libelf_next_arhdr_wrlock(ref)","note":"The file is detected as an ar archive (ELF_K_AR); dup_elf calls next_arhdr to read the first member header."},{"step":4,"file":"libelf/elf_begin.c","function":"__libelf_next_arhdr_wrlock","line":913,"var":"elf->state.ar.long_names","code":"read_long_names(elf)","note":"The first archive member has ar_name starting with / followed by digits (a long name reference), so read_long_names is invoked to locate the // long-names table."},{"step":5,"file":"libelf/elf_begin.c","function":"read_long_names","line":765,"var":"len","code":"len = atol(string)","note":"atol is called on the ar_size field without verifying it starts with a digit; a malformed ar_size yields an unexpected value (e.g. negative or 0)."},{"step":6,"file":"libelf/elf_begin.c","function":"read_long_names","line":771,"var":"offset","code":"offset += sizeof(struct ar_hdr) + ((len + 1) & ~1l)","note":"A negative len from atol causes the offset arithmetic to wrap, making the scan read archive headers from unexpected in-file locations."},{"step":7,"file":"libelf/elf_begin.c","function":"read_long_names","line":790,"var":"newp","code":"newp = malloc(len)","note":"When a // entry is found with a malformed ar_size, malloc is called with a huge size_t (negative len converted to unsigned), and if it succeeds the subsequent memcpy reads out of bounds from the mapped file, causing the ASAN crash."}]' > /workspace/candidate_trace.json
echo "Trace written"
cat /workspace/candidate_trace.json | python3 -m json.tool > /dev/null && echo "Valid JSON"
</parameter>
